## B8.3 Planted-error courses (owner: Student 2), PARTIAL

Variants based on B8.2, each with one known error from the checker catalogue (PRD C2.3), for testing
the Course Checker in Release 1. CK-07 and the proposed CK-08 case instead use the merged course with
the B8.1 template as their baseline.

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Folder | `testdata/b8-3-planted-errors/`; the answer file is `expected-findings.yaml` |
| Source and licence | Fictional, derived from B8.2 (Apache-2.0, the same as the repository). No real learner data |
| Status | **PARTIAL.** 4 of 13 CK rules have built package variants (CK-02, CK-03, CK-09, CK-12). The other 9 CK rule categories require Moodle `.mbz` inputs and are represented by 10 separate variants because CK-06 has two independent cases (duplicate and invalid `idnumber`). All 10 variants are `pending-lab`: no file exists for them |
| What the tests prove | The dataset is well formed and every entry maps to a valid CK rule. **They do not show that the checker detects anything.** No checker exists yet; the 100 % target (PRD C2.7) is measured in Release 1 |

**Layout.** `<variant-id>/package/` is a full copy of the B8.2 package with exactly one file changed.
B8.2 is never changed. The folders `missing-body`, `duplicate-id`, `protected-id` and `invalid-mode`
(PR #118) test the B1 validator, not CK rules, and are listed in its `answer.yaml`.

**CK-08 fixture maker** (`b8-3-planted-errors/make_ck08_fixture.py`, PRD B8.3, C2.3; scripted edit approved
by the guide, issue #232 point 4). It makes the synthetic CK-08 `.mbz` from a **copy** of the merged
B8.2 + B8.1 backup and never touches Moodle:

```bash
python testdata/b8-3-planted-errors/make_ck08_fixture.py --input merged.mbz \
    --target-idnumber wk-01-task --output ck-08.synthetic.mbz   # writes it and <output>.report.json
# add --dry-run to write nothing; run again with --check (no --target-idnumber) to verify the result
```

- It finds the activity ids in the backup itself (`activities/<module>_<cmid>/`); it does not assume
  the B8.1 reference ids. One criterion in `course/completion.xml` gets an id no activity has
  (highest id + 1). The activity stays. No `idnumber` is added. Every other file is copied byte for
  byte and the archive is written deterministically, so the same input gives the same SHA-256.
- The report records the SHA-256 of the input, of `completion.xml` before and after, and of the
  output, and says `fixture: synthetic`. The output name must end in `.synthetic.mbz`.
- It refuses unsafe archive paths, links, duplicates, oversized members and XML with a DOCTYPE or
  ENTITY. It never overwrites a file. **Undo:** delete `<output>` and `<output>.report.json`; the
  input is never modified.
- **Not done here (needs the approved merged backup and a Moodle lab):** running it on the real
  B8.2 + B8.1 backup, and confirming that the result does not also fire CK-07 (by the design §3.4
  boundary it should not: the criterion does not resolve, so it is CK-08's alone and `also_expected`
  stays `[]`). Until then CK-08 stays `assertable: false` and the variant `pending-lab`. The
  tests (`libs/contracts/tests/test_b8_3_ck08_fixture_maker.py`) use a synthetic backup built in a
  temporary folder and say nothing about the real one. The backup layout they assume (course-level
  `course/completion.xml`, `moduleinstance` holding the cmid, `module.xml` with the cmid as `id`)
  must be confirmed on the real B8.1 backup.
- The generated `.mbz` and its report are not committed.

**The mapping is confirmed by the design owner.** Shraddha (@shraddha0103) approved all 14 planted-error variant-to-rule mappings on 2026-11-26 in [PR #148](https://github.com/narenccode/learnops/pull/148#issuecomment-7194780768). The confirmation is recorded in `expected-findings.yaml` and checked by `test_mapping_is_confirmed_by_design_owner`. This confirms the expected-finding mapping only; the checker design remains `Draft`, no checker detection is claimed, and the 100 % target is not yet measured. CK-08 remains `assertable: false` until its scripted fixture is created and verified not to trigger CK-07. CK-12 remains `assertable: false` until the shared extractor is implemented and tested.


**Reading `expected-findings.yaml`.** Each entry gives the variant `id`, the `rule`, the `element`
(by idnumber), the `expected` finding (rule, element, severity), the `reason`, and `also_expected`:
other rules that fire as their own, separate finding on the same variant. A future checker test should
require the `expected` finding and tolerate nothing outside `expected` and `also_expected`. The guide
decided that the root cause is reported once (§12 item 13): an item that is unreachable because of CK-04,
CK-05 or CK-13 is still listed as unreachable with its cause, but it is not a separate CK-01 finding, so
those entries have `also_expected: []` and say "explained by CK-0x" in `notes`. CK-01 still fires on its
own variant, where no other rule explains the item. The mapping comes from `docs/design/checker.md` §11.3
and is confirmed by the design-owner approval recorded above.

## B8.5 Lecture videos (owner: Student 4), COMPLETE

- **Where:** `b8-5-lecture-videos/` (folder layout, recording and hashing steps, and the
  completion checklist in its README). The inventory table below is the only list of lectures.
- **Status:** COMPLETE. Five recordings are listed in the inventory below, from four speakers: 451, 441, 462,
  538 and 488 s, **2380 s in total** (the sum of the Duration column; the durations were supplied by the owner
  as measured with `ffprobe` and rounded down, and were not re-measured by the reviewers). Each lecture has an
  outline and a reference transcript, the transcripts are marked `checked` (the transcript of lecture 02, whose
  speaker is Harshitha, was checked by Nagashree V; the other four by Harshitha), and each of the four speakers
  has written a consent line in decision 0004. These five replace five short clips (338 s) listed earlier, which
  were never accepted as B8.5 evidence. The files are not in Git. The temporary exceptions in decision 0004
  (four lectures, no 1800 s total) are not used. This record does **not** show a word error rate or any G-6
  result: no measurement has been run, and the method and normalisation are still to be approved (App-C 7).
- **Method (guide decision, recorded in `docs/decisions/0004-b8-5-lecture-videos.md`):**
  - at least **5** short technical lectures in **Indian English**, together approximately
    **30 minutes** of recording; the acceptance threshold is a total of at least **1800 s**;
  - recorded by the project team for this project (no faculty or NPTEL recordings); each
    speaker speaks naturally from an outline, not from a script;
  - every speaker writes one consent line (one per speaker, even for several lectures) with
    their own name, the date, and exactly this sentence: "used to test speech recognition; video stays in the lab; transcript published under Apache-2.0";
  - reference transcripts are typed by hand, or corrected by hand from a draft made by a model
    that is not part of our speech-to-text comparison; Harshitha (`Harshithamanjunatha`) checks
    every transcript.
- **Licence:** the published outlines and reference transcripts are Apache-2.0, like the
  repository. The recordings are not published and have no public licence.
- **Stays out of Git:** the video recordings, any audio extracted from them, and any unreviewed
  or model-made transcript draft. They are kept as described in "Original recording storage"
  below. Only outlines and reviewed reference transcripts are committed.
- **PRD note:** PRD §B8 says "≥ 30 min total, enough for the first word-error-rate baseline run, App-C 7" (this text follows
  the guide's answer on issue #186; an earlier version said "Release 0 baseline"), which matches the guide's decision above.

### Original recording storage

- Until the lab storage is ready, each original recording stays on the computer of the team
  member who recorded it, in a folder that is **not** synced to Google Drive, OneDrive or any
  other cloud service. Check that the folder (for example Documents or Desktop) is not being
  backed up to a cloud service.
- Keep recordings outside the repository folder. Do not share them.
- Move them to the lab storage when it becomes available.
- No link to any storage location is written in this repository.
- Tell each speaker about this interim storage before they write their consent line.

What Git ignores, as checked with `git check-ignore`: the root `.gitignore` ignores `*.mp4`,
`*.mov`, `*.mkv` and `*.webm` files and the folders `testdata/media/` and `testdata/downloads/`
anywhere in the repository, but **not** audio files (for example `.wav`, `.mp3` or `.m4a`) or
other video formats (for example `.avi`). Inside `testdata/b8-5-lecture-videos/` only, a folder
`.gitignore` ignores every file except `README.md`, `.gitignore`, `outline.md` and
`transcript.en.txt`.

### Inventory

Values are filled in only from the real recording, the speaker's own consent and the reviewed
transcript. `PENDING` means not known yet. The validation test added with this set
(`libs/contracts/tests/test_b8_5_dataset.py`) reads this table, so keep its structure fixed:

- the ten columns, in this order and with these exact header names;
- one row per lecture; the ID is `lecture-NN` (two digits);
- **Duration (s):** whole seconds (an integer), or `PENDING`;
- **Recording file:** the file name only (no folder, no URL), or `PENDING`;
- **SHA-256:** 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters, or `PENDING`;
- **Outline / Transcript:** paths relative to `testdata/`, in backticks;
- **Consent:** `PENDING` until the lecture's speaker has a consent line in the decision record,
  then `` `0004` speaker-NN `` (that speaker's line; several lectures may share it);
- **Transcript review:** `pending` until Harshitha has checked the transcript, then `checked`.

The **Status** line above says `PENDING` until every row is complete; then it says `COMPLETE`.
The test fails if the status says `COMPLETE` while anything is missing, and also if the data is
complete but the status still says `PENDING`.

**Total recorded duration:** 2380 s (39 min 40 s)

The total is written because the Status is `COMPLETE` (the checker requires a `PENDING` set to keep this line `PENDING`). Duration (s) values above were supplied by the owner as measured with `ffprobe` on the five stored files and rounded down; SHA-256 values and file names were supplied by the owner for the same files (not re-verified here). The minimum-total rule and its temporary exception are in decision 0004.

How the total is calculated: the sum of the `Duration (s)` column, where each duration is the
recording's length measured with `ffprobe` and rounded **down** to whole seconds (so the total is
never overstated). The set needs a total of at least 1800 s. Write it as `<seconds> s (<m> min <s> s)`,
for example `1834 s (30 min 34 s)`.
